site.reason: Python reads whole lines; Java Scanner reads whitespace-separated tokens, and nextLine() after nextInt() returns the rest of the current line, often an empty string.

Because no nextInt() or next() precedes line 13, nextLine() consumes the full first line rather than a leftover newline, matching Python's input().

site.reason: split() with no argument treats any run of whitespace as one separator and drops leading and trailing empties; Java split(" ") splits on every single space and keeps a leading empty string.

flags.assumption: The expression scanner.nextLine().split(" ") on line 14 assumes the input line has no leading spaces, trailing spaces, consecutive spaces, tabs, or empty lines; otherwise split(" ") produces empty strings or unsplit whitespace that cause Integer::parseInt on line 15 to throw NumberFormatException.
flags.suggestion: Replace scanner.nextLine().split(" ") on line 14 with scanner.nextLine().split("\\s+") and insert .filter(str -> !str.isEmpty()) before .mapToInt(Integer::parseInt).
flags.reasoning: Python's input().split() splits on arbitrary runs of whitespace and discards leading/trailing whitespace as well as empty results on blank lines. Java's split(" ") splits only on single space characters, keeping leading empty strings (e.g., " 1 2") or consecutive empty strings (e.g., "1  2") and failing on tabs, causing Integer::parseInt to throw.

site.reason: Python ints have unlimited precision; Java int and long arithmetic wraps silently on overflow (1000000 * 1000000 as an int is -727379968).

flags.assumption: The comparison a[i] < a[i - 1] * 2 uses 32-bit int arithmetic on int[] elements, assuming that a[i - 1] * 2 does not overflow 32-bit int, though no input range is stated in the code; for input values such as 1500000000 and 2000000000, a[i - 1] * 2 overflows to -1294967296 and Java outputs NO while Python outputs YES.
flags.suggestion: Change a[i - 1] * 2 on line 19 to a[i - 1] * 2L (or use BigInteger for the array elements if inputs themselves can exceed int/long).
flags.reasoning: Python integers have arbitrary precision, so a[i - 1] * 2 never overflows. In Java, a is int[] and 2 is an int literal, so a[i - 1] * 2 overflows silently when a[i - 1] > 1073741823 or a[i - 1] < -1073741824. Using 2L widens the multiplication to 64-bit long so it cannot overflow for any 32-bit int array element.
